message:
This PR removes the deprecated "multiapi" functionality from the TypeSpec Python HTTP client generator as requested in issue #8310.

## Changes Made

### Core Option Removal
- Removed `multiapi` from the default options dictionary
- Removed multiapi validation logic from `_validate_combinations` method
- Added deprecation handling that always returns `False` for the multiapi option (maintaining backward compatibility)

### Model Classes
- Removed `imports_for_multiapi` methods from all model classes:
  - `Client`, `Config`, `OperationBase`, `OperationGroup`
  - `BaseType`, `ConstantType`, `Parameter`, `Response` classes
- Updated class name generation logic to remove multiapi-specific behavior

### Serializers
- Removed multiapi-specific code generation logic from all serializers
- Removed multiapi filtering for samples and tests
- Simplified namespace configuration by removing multiapi path handling
- Removed conditional metadata generation for multiapi
- Updated template parameter passing to remove multiapi API version handling

### Templates
- Updated Jinja2 templates to remove multiapi-specific code blocks
- Removed conditional API version parameter passing
- Simplified operation group initialization

### File Removal
- Deleted `metadata_serializer.py` (contained exclusively multiapi functionality)

### Documentation
- Updated help text in CI scripts to remove multiapi references

## Backward Compatibility

The multiapi option is still accepted but deprecated. When accessed, it always returns `False` regardless of the value set, effectively disabling all multiapi functionality while maintaining compatibility with existing configurations that may still reference this option.

## Testing

Verified that:
- The multiapi option always returns `False` when accessed
- Other configuration options continue to work normally
- Default values are preserved for all remaining options
- Core functionality imports work correctly

Fixes #8310.
